title: Control Coverage Map
description: Every kill chain has a 'How to Defend' section — this graph is that library read backwards. Nodes are the ~19 controls those sections actually recommend, plus the 45 incidents themselves. An edge from a control to an incident means that control, sourced from that incident's own defend section, would have broken its chain. Select a control to see exactly how many of the 45 real breaches it would have stopped — a control's blast radius here is a defensive coverage number, not an attack path.

nodes.label: Enforce MFA everywhere (phishing-resistant where humans log in)
Segment high-value systems from the rest
Take admin/ERP/MFT systems off the public internet; patch fast
Out-of-band callback verification for phone-based requests
Inventory & govern every OAuth app / connected integration
Get long-lived secrets out of CI/CD; scan and scope everywhere
Pin dependencies by hash; disable install scripts
Verify build provenance; build from source, not a tarball
Maintain a live SBOM / dependency inventory
Alert on anomalous data-access or export volume
Constrain what AI agents can reach
Govern fourth-party/vendor access as your own attack surface
Keep immutable, offline backups; rehearse the restore

links.tech: "Implement a call-back verification procedure for any credential or access request by phone."
"Enforce IMDSv2 on all EC2 instances."
"Apply least-privilege IAM to every role." (independently sufficient)
"Implement software supply chain integrity verification for build systems."
"Detect Golden SAML by correlating ADFS event logs with Azure AD sign-in logs."
"Rotate long-lived service keys on a schedule, because that is the one lever you hold."
"Stop putting long-lived secrets in the CI environment at all."
"Take RMM and management consoles off the public internet."
"Keep immutable, offline backups and rehearse the restore."
"Generate and keep an SBOM for everything you build and everything you run."
"Build from the repository, not from tarballs, and verify the two match."
"Restrict access by device posture as well as identity" — FIDO2 key stopped it at Cloudflare
"Restrict access by device posture as well as identity, so a stolen session is not enough."
"Bind sessions to a device, so a stolen cookie is useless elsewhere."
"Use short-lived, federated credentials in CI instead of stored static secrets."
"Never store production credentials in personal vaults on unmanaged devices."
"Map the fourth party, at least for critical vendors."
"Ask your identity provider who else can reset your users' MFA."
"Never hardcode credentials in scripts - use dynamic secrets from your PAM."
"Segment your network so contractor VPNs cannot reach all internal shares."
"Treat the build environment as your most sensitive production system, not as developer infrastructure."
"Break the personal-device-to-corporate-network path, because that is where the cascade crossed."
"Take managed file transfer off the open internet, or put it behind authentication you control."
"Run secret scanning across all repositories including SAS token patterns."
"Audit OAuth application permissions and expire the ones nobody can justify."
"Enforce MFA on every internet-facing access path, and audit for the ones you have forgotten."
"Segment so that one remote access foothold cannot reach everything."
"Eliminate long-lived IAM access keys and rotate what remains."
"Enable S3 Versioning and Object Lock, and keep isolated backups."
"Reduce standing Global Administrator, since impersonation targets whoever holds the role."
"Pin dependencies by hash and treat a new transitive dependency as a reviewable change."
"Bound agent objectives explicitly, because an open-ended goal will be pursued anywhere it leads."
"Stop keeping publishing tokens in jobs that run third-party tooling."
"Compare the artifact against the source of truth before you trust it."
"Get long-lived cloud credentials out of CI entirely."
"Publish from CI with Trusted Publishing, and verify provenance on the way in."
"Use npm trusted publishing with environment protection rules and required reviewers."
"Pin every action to a full 40-character commit SHA and pin your own dependencies with a lockfile."
"Phishing-resistant MFA on maintainer accounts, because TOTP was relayed in real time."
"Pin dependencies by hash and add a publication delay."
"Treat installed AI agents as a credential-access surface with their own threat model."
"Rotate credentials on day one, and treat 'we installed a bad package' as credential compromise."
"Bind session tokens so a stolen one is useless elsewhere."
"Monitor your identity provider yourself; your vendor's detection is not yours."
"Get the ERP off the internet, because attack-surface reduction is the only control that works before a patch exists."
"Self-host third-party scripts, or pin them with Subresource Integrity."
"Require explicit user confirmation before any agentic tool execution involving external apps."
"Inventory and scope every third-party OAuth integration connected to your SaaS tenants."
"Assume any exposed key is burned and rotate downstream credentials."
"Segment your ESXi environment from the corporate identity plane."
"Run tabletop exercises specifically for the 'help desk social engineering to Okta to cloud' scenario."
"Disable install scripts, and pin dependencies by hash."
"Replace long-lived publish tokens with short-lived, scoped, provenance-backed publishing."
"Get on-premises collaboration servers off the public internet."
"Rotate the machine keys, then restart IIS - patching alone leaves the attacker inside."
"Enforce MFA on all Snowflake accounts - especially service accounts."
"Protect crash dump pipelines - scan for key material before copying to non-isolated environments."
"Treat self-service password reset as a credential-issuance system and protect it like one."
"Gate the registration flow itself with Conditional Access."
"Minimize and scope the secrets exposed to CI jobs."
"Pin third-party Actions to a full commit SHA, not a mutable tag."
"Finish credential migrations by revoking the old credential."
"Allowlist connected apps, and restrict who can authorize one."
"Harden the human process the same way you would a technical one."
"Inventory and govern OAuth grants as identity infrastructure, because that is what they are."
"Extend vendor risk to the fourth party and make revocation a drill."
"Replace standing tokens with short-lived, source-bound credentials."
"Retire long-lived access keys entirely."
"Correlate CloudTrail across accounts on source IP and user agent, not one account at a time."
"Constrain what your own agents can reach, since a jailbroken agent inherits every capability you gave it."
"Alert on anomalous S3 access volume."
"Alert on anomalous PAM admin logins immediately."
"Alert on anomalous S3 access patterns from production credential use."
"Monitor Snowflake QUERY_HISTORY for COPY INTO external stage operations."
"Alert on data volume, because everything else looks legitimate."
"Alert on export volume, because the credential and the app will both look legitimate."
"Apply least-privilege Snowflake roles."
